title: Study: Smoking May Increase Risk of Schizophrenia

image.attribution: Lindsay Fox from Newport beach, United States / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-2.0

main_content:
Studies have linked cigarette smoking to a number of health problems, including lung cancer and heart disease. Now, a new study shows a possible link between smoking and the disabling brain disorder schizophrenia. People with schizophrenia hear and see things that are not real.

Cigarette smoking is very common among people with mental disorders, especially those with schizophrenia. Sameer Jauhar noted the connection.

Sameer Jauhar is a psychiatric researcher at King’s College London.

Dr. Jauhar and a King’s College team found that smoking may in some way increase the risk of developing schizophrenia. They found that smoking is three times more common among schizophrenic patients.

James MacCabe was one of the writers of a report on the study. He is a doctor of psychiatric research at King’s College. He says the finding raises questions about the belief that people who have mental disorders smoke to ease their symptoms.

James MacCabe says there is not enough evidence yet to confirm the link between cigarette smoking and the development of schizophrenia.

questions.question: What health problems have studies linked smoking to?
options: A) Lung cancer and heart disease
B) High blood pressure and diabetes
questions.answer: A) Lung cancer and heart disease

questions.question: Who is James MacCabe?
options: A) A psychologist at King’s College
B) A doctor of psychiatric research at King’s College
questions.answer: B) A doctor of psychiatric research at King’s College

questions.question: Has the link between smoking and schizophrenia been confirmed?
options: A) Yes, it has been definitively confirmed
B) No, there is not enough evidence yet
C) Yes, but only in specific populations
D) No, it has been disproven
questions.answer: B) No, there is not enough evidence yet
